transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
House Republicans have scuttled an impeachment effort targeting Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth,
the vote to effectively block impeachment charges from being considered passed 211 to
204.
Here's NPR's Eric McDaniel.
>> Kentucky Republican Representative Thomas Massie spearheaded this impeachment effort
on his way out of Congress.
And the charges he filed were tied to failure to get congressional approval for military
action in Iran and Yemen, as well as strikes against what the administration says are drug
boats in the Caribbean and Pacific, and a Pentagon effort to publish a Democratic Senator,
Mark Kelly of Arizona, who told service members not to follow illegal orders.
Hegseth called the charges a sham, and the White House backed him up.
Most Republicans, even those openly critical of the administration's relationship with
Congress in terms of war powers, agree.
The impeachment effort is now dead.
Eric McDaniel, NPR News, Capitol Hill.
>> Republicans have chosen their leaders for the new Congress that will convene in January.
Senate Republicans today opted to keep John Thune of South Dakota as their leader.
On the House side, Republicans chose Judiciary Committee Chairman and Trump ally Jim Jordan
of Ohio.
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer says he's confident that he'll keep his job as
the top Democrat in January when the party retakes a majority.
>> Both independents, Senator Bernie Sanders and Democrat Alyssa Slotkin, though, have
come out against Schumer's NPR's Elena Moore reports.
>> Sanders, an independent who caucuses with the Democrats, told reporters that he believes
a major takeaway from the midterms is that voters want the party to move in a new direction.
>> I personally have known Chuck Schumer for over 30 years.
And I like Chuck, nobody who works harder than Chuck Schumer.
But in my view, the time is now for change.
>> Senator Alyssa Slotkin echoed that, calling for colleagues to publicly challenge Schumer
and propose a plan for the first 100 days that makes good on voter calls to govern differently.
It comes as a handful of incoming Senate Democrats have also declined to back Schumer for the
top job.
Elena Moore, NPR News.
>> Drivers got some relief today.
For the first time in months, average pump prices fell below $4 a gallon.
NPR's Willa Rubin reports on what's behind the drop.
>> It's normal for the price of gas to tick down in the fall.
Peak driving season has ended, and refineries are finishing their annual maintenance.
So there's a little more gas to go around.
But here is the big reason.
Right now, Brent crude is getting cheaper.
This is what refineries need to make gasoline, also diesel and jet fuel.
A barrel of Brent now costs about $90.
Average prices are trading lower because there's a bit more oil flowing out of the Middle East.
But a gallon of gas still costs a dollar more than a year ago.
AAA says the price of the pump is still the highest ever for this time of the year.
Willa Rubin, NPR News.
>> And you're listening to NPR News.
A handwritten copy of Martin Luther King Jr's I Have a Dream speech is going up for auction
early next year.
And NPR's Jason Derose reports on the newly identified draft.
>> Martin Luther King spoke on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial in 1963 during the March
on Washington.
Christie's in New York is auctioning off the seven yellow legal pad pages covered in blue
cursive.
Some lines scratched out, others scribbled in the margins.
Researchers recently discovered the draft among the papers of one of King's advisors
and believe it was written in the early morning hours on the day the speech was delivered.
Christie says this draft was previously unknown to scholars and that the last minute edits
offer insights into King's creative process.
The auction house says a portion of the proceeds will go to the Martin Luther King Jr center
for nonviolent social change.
Jason Derose, NPR News.
>> Several members of the Kennedy family are joining efforts aimed at stopping President
Trump from building his proposed triumphal arch in Washington, DC.
They filed documents today to join a court case against the arch saying it would obstruct
views and cast shadows over their relatives' graves.
Construction is currently on hold.
A judge issued a temporary order blocking it through November 19th.
Stocks in Asia mixed in Wednesday trading after Wall Street lost ground following the
latest reading on inflation.
New data from the Labor Department shows inflation ran hotter than expected last month, contributing
to investor expectations at the Federal Reserve will raise its benchmark interest rate next
month.
I'm Giles Snyder.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: House Republicans defeat Thomas Massie's effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, 211-204
Senate Republicans keep John Thune as leader; House Republicans choose Jim Jordan
Bernie Sanders and Alyssa Slotkin call for change as Chuck Schumer seeks to keep Democratic leadership
Average US gas prices fall below $4 a gallon for first time in months as Brent crude drops
Handwritten draft of Martin Luther King Jr.'s I Have a Dream speech to be auctioned by Christie's
Kennedy family joins court case opposing Trump's proposed triumphal arch in Washington, DC
Stocks in Asia mixed after Wall Street falls on hotter-than-expected inflation report
